result.title: More Powerful, Less Verifiable? Mitigating Hard-to-Verify Hallucinations in MLLM's Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) strengthens model capabilities through feedback from humans and environments. However, emerging evidence suggests that reward optimization can produce outputs whose errors are harder for humans to detect. To address this issue, we construct ITHV (the Image-Text Hallucination Verifiability Dataset), comprising 2,728 visually grounded instances that distinguish between obvious hallucinations, which humans readily detect, and elusive hallucinations, which humans struggle to identify. We then propose DAPO-V, an extension of DAPO that maximizes correctness subject to a budget on verifiability-aware risk. Specifically, DAPO-V combines a verifiability-aware reward with adaptive dual control, where larger penalties are assigned to incorrect responses on questions with lower human verification accuracy. An adaptive multiplier further adjusts the penalty strength according to risk-budget violations. Across three MLLM base models, DAPO-V improves overall accuracy while substantially improving accuracy on elusive hallucination questions by 5.78--9.72 percentage points over accuracy-only DAPO. We further test DAPO-V with a blinded human study, which shows that hallucinations are more readily detected in DAPO-V than those of the base model.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建了区分「明显」与「隐蔽」幻觉的图文数据集 ITHV，并提出 DAPO-V，在可验证性感知的风险预算约束下用自适应双重控制加大对人难以察觉错误的惩罚，以缓解 RL 后难以核验的幻觉。
AI.relevance_reason: 对隐蔽幻觉的区分可作为「视觉证据是否被真正使用」的评测与失败分析资源，其可验证性加权奖励也可供核查 latent 视觉接地与监督分配的线索；但该方法只在输出奖励层面施加约束，未涉及推理期 latent 状态。
